what_its_for: Pitavastatin is used to lower bad cholesterol (LDL) and fats (triglycerides) in your blood, and to raise good cholesterol (HDL). It helps reduce your risk of heart attack, stroke, and other heart problems. It works best when combined with a healthy diet and exercise.
how_to_take: Take pitavastatin by mouth once daily with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole. You can take it at any time of day, but try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember. Do not crush or chew the tablet.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 2 mg once daily. Your doctor may adjust your dose based on how your body responds and your cholesterol levels. The maximum dose is 4 mg once daily. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for your dose.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — unless it is almost time for your next dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at once to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store pitavastatin at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking large amounts of grapefruit juice, as it may increase the amount of this medicine in your blood. Avoid alcohol or limit its use, since heavy drinking can raise the risk of liver problems. Do not take cyclosporine (an immune-suppressing drug) with pitavastatin, as this combination is not safe. Tell your doctor about all other medications and supplements you take, especially other cholesterol medicines, certain antibiotics like erythromycin, and blood thinners like warfarin.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: unexplained muscle pain, tenderness, weakness, or cramps (especially with fever or dark-colored urine, which could be a sign of a rare but serious muscle condition called rhabdomyolysis); yellowing of your skin or eyes, dark urine, or severe stomach pain (possible signs of liver problems); unusual tiredness; or any signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing. Also tell your doctor if you become pregnant while taking this medication.
when_it_works: Pitavastatin starts working soon after you begin taking it, but you may not feel any different because high cholesterol usually has no symptoms. Your doctor will check your cholesterol levels with a blood test after about 4 weeks to see how well the medicine is working. It is important to keep taking it even if you feel fine.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Do NOT take pitavastatin if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as it can harm the unborn baby. Use effective birth control while taking this medicine. Do not breastfeed while taking pitavastatin. Children: Safety and dosing in children have not been fully established; talk to your doctor. Older adults: Older patients may be at a slightly higher risk of muscle side effects; your doctor will monitor you closely. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as your dose may need to be adjusted or pitavastatin may not be right for you.
